summary: Eligible PICS retry rows could starve behind an older pending backlog because claim_work compared next_attempt_at before distinguishing retrying from pending. The fix prefers retrying rows only after preserving lane and priority precedence.
why_this_tier: Database correctness contributed +2, the external background worker contributed +1, and the already isolated owning function contributed -1. The database-correctness override required three independent read-only assessments.
observed_facts: claim_work filters pending and retrying rows together but orders lane, priority, next_attempt_at, dirty_since, and ID without a state preference.
The processor calls claim_work separately for the live/new lane group and the catch-up lane, so lane quotas remain isolated.
At 2026-07-25T07:21:40.498166Z, live Tiger had 281353 catch-up pending rows and 31 catch-up retrying rows at priority 100.
The catch-up pending rows had next_attempt_at 2026-07-25T03:23:23.169921Z, earlier than every retry row, so the current first 20 candidates contained zero retries.
Live Tiger also had 876 live pending rows and 35 live retrying rows at priority 200.
The three claims interrupted by the approved quota redeploy remained eligible attempts 1/8 lease_expired retries.
The current and proposed query plans have the same parallel sequential-scan, bounded-sort, and gather-merge shape; estimated cost changed by less than one percent.
The targeted durable-work baseline passed 14 tests before the fix.
The fix adds retry-state ordering after lane and priority and before next_attempt_at.
The post-fix targeted suite passed 15 tests and the complete PICS suite passed 102 tests.

reproduction_status.summary: Live Tiger and a minimal ordering simulation both show an equally prioritized pending row with an older next_attempt_at is selected before an eligible retry row.

db_checks.purpose: Prove the current claim order starves eligible retries behind same-lane, same-priority pending work.
db_checks.sql: SELECT lane, priority, state, count(*) AS rows, min(next_attempt_at), max(next_attempt_at) FROM ops.pics_work_state WHERE stream_key='primary' AND state IN ('pending','retrying') GROUP BY lane, priority, state ORDER BY lane, priority DESC, state LIMIT 30;
db_checks.result_summary: Catch-up had 281353 pending and 31 retrying rows at priority 100. Every pending row's next_attempt_at preceded the retry rows, and the current first 20 ordered candidates were all pending.

db_checks.purpose: Compare current and proposed query-plan cost before choosing whether a new index or migration is required.
db_checks.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT work.id FROM ops.pics_work_state work WHERE work.work_mode='durable' AND work.stream_key='primary' AND work.lane=ANY(ARRAY['catchup']::text[]) AND work.state IN ('pending','retrying') AND work.next_attempt_at<=clock_timestamp() AND work.attempts<work.max_attempts ORDER BY CASE work.lane WHEN 'new' THEN 0 WHEN 'live' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END, work.priority DESC, CASE work.state WHEN 'retrying' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, work.next_attempt_at, work.dirty_since, work.id LIMIT 40;
db_checks.result_summary: The proposed state tie-breaker retained the current plan shape and changed estimated cost by less than one percent, so no new index or schema migration is justified.

root_cause_hypotheses.label: Missing retry-state tie-breaker
root_cause_hypotheses.evidence: The owning SQL admits both states but orders next_attempt_at before any state distinction; live data has an older pending timestamp across the backlog and therefore excludes retries from the bounded claim.

fix_options.title: Add retry-before-pending after lane and priority
fix_options.summary: Insert a deterministic retry-state CASE after priority and before next_attempt_at in the existing candidate ORDER BY.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Smallest change; preserves lane, priority, quotas, leases, and response shapes. Equally prioritized fresh pending work is delayed by the bounded number of eligible retries.

fix_options.title: Split retry and pending candidates with a new retry index
fix_options.summary: Claim retries and pending work through separate candidate CTEs backed by an additive partial index.
fix_options.tradeoffs: More code and a production schema migration for no demonstrated plan benefit at current scale.

fix_options.title: Leave ordering unchanged and repair queues operationally
fix_options.summary: Keep the current SQL and manually requeue or reprioritize retry rows.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Does not fix the defect, violates durable queue ownership, requires repeated production writes, and risks inconsistent reconciliation.

recommended_fix: Add retry-before-pending as a tie-breaker only after lane and priority in claim_work, with regression coverage proving lane and priority remain ahead of state and retry state remains ahead of next_attempt_at. No schema migration is needed.
verification_plan: Add a targeted SQL-order regression test in test_durable_work.py.

residual_risks: A burst of eligible retries can temporarily displace equally prioritized fresh pending work within the same lane, but the existing per-lane quota and max-attempt controls remain bounded.
Existing production retries will not drain under the new order until a separately approved deployment uses the fix.
The current claim query already uses a sequential scan and bounded sort; this fix does not address broader future queue-scale optimization.
